articles.title: Shohei Ohtani 'Not 100%' Yet, Will Not Pitch vs. Tigers On Sunday
articles.summary: Shohei Ohtani will not pitch Sunday against the Detroit Tigers after experiencing knee discomfort during a Friday bullpen session.
articles.body: Shohei Ohtani will not pitch Sunday against the Detroit Tigers after experiencing knee discomfort during a Friday bullpen session. Los Angeles Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said before Saturday’s 2-1 loss that Ohtani’s knee still isn’t pain free, and he’s also having minor issues with the biceps muscle that troubled him earlier in the inning. After the game, Roberts said Ohtani would not be used against Detroit and his next pitching outing is up in the air. Tyler Glasnow, who was expected to follow Ohtani, will now start Sunday’s game. The two-way star hasn’t pitched since throwing six innings in a 4-3 win against the San Diego Padres on July 3, and would have only pitched an inning or two on Sunday. "The hard part right now is trying to figure out if he’s not 100% in the overall body, is it worth giving him an inning to build him up," Roberts asked. Ohtani has been able to hit through the problems - he’s batting .274 with 12 homers in 45 games since his last pitching performance - and the addition of Tarik Skubal has made it easier to win without him in the rotation. Reporting by The Associated Press.

articles.title: Inspiring story on parenthood: “I gave up my childhood to be able to have my children’s childhood” – What Andre Agassi and wife Steffi Graf’s parenting journey teaches about raising a family
articles.summary: International Sports News: Andre Agassi’s words, “I gave up my childhood to be able to have my children’s childhood,” offer a deeply personal look at how becoming a parent chang.
articles.body: Andre Agassi’s words, “I gave up my childhood to be able to have my children’s childhood,” offer a deeply personal look at how becoming a parent changed the tennis legend’s view of his own life. Agassi grew up in a world where tennis was not simply a sport but a major part of his everyday life, with intense training and expectations starting at a very young age. Years later, after becoming one of tennis’ biggest stars, he and his wife, fellow tennis legend Steffi Graf, built a family life around their two children, Jaden and Jaz. For Agassi, watching his children grow gave him the chance to experience some of the simple moments of childhood that he felt he had missed himself.What did Andre Agassi mean when he said, “I gave up my childhood to be able to have my children’s childhood”?The quote is closely connected to Agassi’s own experience growing up. He started playing tennis as a young child and was pushed toward the sport by his father, Mike Agassi. His father had a clear dream for him: he wanted his son to become one of the best tennis players in the world.That dream eventually came true.Agassi went on to become world No. 1 and won eight Grand Slam singles titles during his career. But reaching that level meant spending much of his childhood training, competing and preparing for professional tennis.For a young child, that kind of life can leave little room for ordinary experiences. Instead of having complete freedom to decide how he wanted to spend his time, Agassi’s days were largely connected to tennis.That is where his famous quote becomes especially powerful.When he says he “gave up” his childhood, he is looking back at the years he spent becoming a professional athlete. But he is also talking about what those sacrifices eventually allowed him to do.His success gave him the freedom to step away from tennis and spend more time with his family. It allowed him to be present as his children grew up.In other words, Agassi may have missed parts of his own childhood, but later he had the opportunity to sit beside his children and watch them experience theirs. For him, that became a kind of second chance.How did becoming a father change Agassi’s view of his own childhood?Fatherhood gave Agassi a different way of looking at his past. When he watched Jaden and Jaz grow up, he could see the small moments of childhood from a parent’s point of view.He could watch them discover what they liked, make their own choices and develop personalities separate from their famous parents.Those moments were very different from the childhood Agassi had experienced.His early years were strongly connected to the tennis court. His father believed that constant practice and discipline were necessary if Agassi was going to become a champion. That approach helped produce an incredible tennis career, but it also meant that Agassi’s childhood was far from ordinary.As a father, he wanted something different for his children.Instead of seeing childhood as preparation for a future career, Agassi wanted Jaden and Jaz to enjoy the years they were living through.That is one of the most important ideas behind his quote. He was not simply saying that he wanted to give his children more material things or better opportunities. He wanted to give them time.Time to grow.Time to explore.Time to make mistakes.Time to decide what they wanted for themselves.This became especially important because Agassi knew from personal experience how powerful parental expectations can be. He had spent years trying to become the player his father wanted him to be. As a parent, he had the chance to make sure his own children did not feel that same pressure.How did Steffi Graf fit into Agassi’s approach to raising their children?Steffi Graf’s role in the family’s story is important because she understood Agassi’s world better than almost anyone. Like her husband, Graf was introduced to tennis at a very young age and went on to become one of the greatest players in the history of the sport.Graf won 22 Grand Slam singles titles and spent years at the top of women’s tennis before retiring in 1999. Agassi and Graf later married and raised their two children, Jaden and Jaz.Together, they had something unusual in common: both parents knew exactly what it took to become a tennis champion, but they also knew the pressure that came with that journey.That understanding appears to have influenced the way they raised their children.Despite having two parents who were global tennis stars, Jaden and Jaz were not simply expected to follow the same path.Jaden developed a passion for baseball rather than choosing tennis as his main sport. Jaz has also been able to follow her own interests. Agassi and Graf have supported their children without making their parents’ careers the center of their lives.That is particularly meaningful when viewed alongside Agassi’s quote.The couple had already achieved what many athletes spend their entire lives chasing. They did not need their children to continue that legacy for them.Instead, they could give their children something that both parents understood the value of: choice.Agassi has also spoken warmly about Graf and the role she plays in his life. Their shared experience in professional sports gave them an understanding of the demands and sacrifices that come with elite competition.For their family, giving their children the freedom to choose their own paths became more important than creating another generation of tennis champions.What does Agassi’s quote tell us about his idea of parenthood?At its heart, Agassi’s quote is about turning his own difficult experiences into something positive for his children.He cannot go back and change the childhood he had. He cannot erase the years of training, pressure and expectations that came with becoming a tennis player.But he can choose what kind of childhood his own children experience.That is what makes the quote about much more than tennis.Many parents work hard because they want their children to have opportunities they did not have themselves. Agassi’s story takes that idea one step further. His goal was not simply to provide his children with a comfortable life. He wanted to be present for the experiences that make childhood special.His words also show that parenthood can change the way people understand their own past.The same childhood that once felt difficult to Agassi became part of what helped him understand his children better. His experiences taught him what pressure can feel like, which may have made him more aware of the importance of giving his own children freedom.And Steffi Graf was there beside him, bringing her own experience as a former champion and a parent.Together, Agassi and Graf chose not to make their children’s lives about living up to their parents’ names. They allowed Jaden and Jaz to build identities of their own.That may be the most powerful part of Agassi’s words.He spent his childhood becoming a tennis champion. But when he became a father, he did not want his children to spend their childhood becoming something for him.He wanted to watch them simply be children.So, when Agassi says, “I gave up my childhood to be able to have my children’s childhood,” he is not only talking about sacrifice. He is talking about perspective, presence and love.He gave years of his life to tennis. Those years helped him become a champion and eventually gave him the freedom to step back and focus on his family.For Agassi, one of the greatest rewards was not another trophy or achievement. It was being able to watch his children grow up on their own terms, with Graf by his side.That is what makes his quote so relatable. Parenthood does not allow us to rewrite our own childhoods, but it can give us the chance to create a different childhood for the next generation.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Chicago Blackhawks urged to acquire skilled defenseman and free agent Nick Blankenburg ahead of the 2026-27 NHL season
articles.summary: NHL News: The Chicago Blackhawks are urged to make an addition to their blue line before the 2026-27 NHL season, and are asked to consider free-agent defenseman.
articles.body: The Chicago Blackhawks are urged to make an addition to their blue line before the 2026-27 NHL season, and are asked to consider free-agent defenseman Nick Blankenburg. Chicago has already been one of the more active teams this offseason. The club has added players like Patrick Kane, Bowen Byram, Jordan Greenway, Ian Cole, and Cole Smith. These trade moves indicate that the Blackhawks are determined to become more competitive after several difficult seasons.Why are the Chicago Blackhawks urged to consider free-agent defenseman Nick Blankenburg?The Chicago Blackhawks are urged to make an intriguing move for skilled defenseman Nick Blankenburg, as reported by several NHL experts. This opinion came during the time when the Blackhawks are considering to add some addition depth to their defensive roster. According to a recent article for Pro Hockey Rumors, Ethan Hetu urged the Blackhawks to make a push for free agent defenseman Nick Blankenburg.Hetu stated, “The Chicago Blackhawks could also be a fit, as they’re slated to rely on a pair of ascending young right-shot defensemen in Sam Rinzel and Artyom Levshunov. Adding Blankenburg would provide the team with capable veteran cover for their right side in case one of those two defensemen endures more growing pains at the NHL level.”Blankenburg's ability to move the puck and contribute offensively could make him particularly attractive. In 61 games during the 2025-26 campaign while splitting time between the Nashville Predators and Colorado Avalanche, he established career highs across the board, recording eight goals, 16 assists and 24 points.Given his excellent calibre and performance, he could compete for a bottom-pairing role while also serving as a seventh defenseman if Chicago's younger players need additional time to develop.With the Blackhawks needing more blueline depth, it would be interesting to see them bring in an offensive defenseman like Blankenburg on a one-year deal, as Chicago signing Blankenburg to an inexpensive one-year deal would add depth without requiring a major long-term commitment.Apart from this, the team has already added players like Patrick Kane, Bowen Byram, Jordan Greenway, Ian Cole, and Cole Smith to their roster. An addition of Blankenburg would give Chicago a regular spot, provide power-play help when needed, and step into the lineup if injuries occur. Also, opting for Nick would be a relatively low-risk move that gives the club additional depth while its young defensive prospects continue developing.For Blankenburg, Chicago could offer an opportunity to establish himself as a reliable NHL defenseman following a career year. So far, there is no indication that a deal is imminent, but if Chicago wants one more intriguing player, Blankenburg would suit the club best, adding further depth to their blueline and their roster as well.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Inspiring story of the day: “My dad had four jobs at one time just to keep me karting” - How Lewis Hamilton and his father turned second-hand kart, and family sacrifice into F1 immortality
articles.summary: International Sports News: Lewis Hamilton’s Formula 1 success did not start with fame, money or a big racing team. It began when he was a child in Stevenage, with his father Ant.
articles.body: Lewis Hamilton’s Formula 1 success did not start with fame, money or a big racing team. It began when he was a child in Stevenage, with his father Anthony Hamilton doing whatever he could to keep his son’s karting dream alive. Anthony worked several jobs while also acting as Lewis’s mechanic and helping him travel to races. Hamilton has said his father’s work ethic and advice stayed with him as he moved into Formula 1. Their professional relationship later became difficult, but the two eventually rebuilt their bond. The story behind Hamilton’s rise remains closely tied to the sacrifices his family made.How did Anthony Hamilton help Lewis Hamilton start his karting careerLewis Hamilton was eight when his father began managing his racing career, and Anthony quickly became much more than a parent watching from the sidelines. He helped prepare the kart, travelled with Lewis and worked to find the money needed to keep him racing.In a 2023 interview discussed by PlanetF1, Hamilton explained just how much his father was doing at the time. “My dad had four jobs at one stage just to keep us go-karting because, when we started karting, the majority of the people were from working-class families,” Hamilton said.That early life was very hands-on. Hamilton also explained that Anthony was his mechanic and that the family travelled together for race weekends. His stepmother, Linda, helped make sure the family had what they needed while they were on the road.Anthony’s role was not simply about finding money. He was also learning how to work on the kart and helping Lewis compete against drivers who had greater access to equipment and mechanics. That experience gave Hamilton an early understanding of how much work went into staying in racing.The sacrifice was especially important because karting can be expensive, and young drivers need regular races and equipment to keep progressing. Anthony did not have the resources of wealthy families in the sport, so the family had to make the opportunity work with what they had.What did Lewis Hamilton learn from his father about racism and racingHamilton also grew up dealing with racism and bullying while competing in motorsport. He has spoken about being the only Black family at some racing events and about being made to feel that he did not belong.His father’s response became one of the most important lessons in Hamilton’s career.In an interview with BBC Sport, Hamilton said: “It’s just how my dad raised me. He said to always do your talking on the track.”The advice was simple: do not waste energy trying to answer people with words. Prove yourself through your driving.Hamilton has described being bullied both at school and on the karting circuit. Instead of allowing those experiences to take him away from racing, he used them as motivation to become better.That mindset followed him into Formula 1. Even after reaching the sport’s biggest stage, Hamilton continued to speak about letting his results answer his critics.His father’s influence was therefore not limited to the practical side of racing. Anthony helped shape the attitude Lewis carried into a career where he would face pressure, criticism and scrutiny at almost every stage.Why did Lewis Hamilton and Anthony Hamilton stop working togetherThe father-son partnership changed once Lewis reached Formula 1. Anthony managed his son through his early years in the sport, including Hamilton’s breakthrough with McLaren and his first world championship in 2008.But in 2010, Lewis decided that his father should no longer manage his professional career.Hamilton was 25 at the time and said the change was needed so the two could have a healthier relationship away from business. The decision did not mean Anthony stopped being important to him. In fact, Hamilton said he wanted his father to simply be his dad.Autosport reported the management change in 2010 after speaking exclusively with Hamilton. He explained that he wanted someone else to handle the professional side while he and his father could focus on their family relationship.The split was not completely easy. The Guardian reported that the two did not speak for several weeks after the professional separation. Hamilton later acknowledged that their relationship had gone through a difficult period.By 2020, however, Hamilton spoke openly about how they had worked to rebuild their bond. BBC Sport reported that he described their journey as difficult and said they had both wanted their father-son relationship back.That part of the story matters because Anthony’s role in Hamilton’s career was never only about management. For years, he had been his father, mechanic, mentor and guide at the same time.How did Lewis Hamilton’s family sacrifice connect to his seven F1 titlesHamilton’s first Formula 1 world title came in 2008, only a year after he made his F1 debut. Twelve years later, he matched Michael Schumacher’s record of seven world championships by winning the 2020 Turkish Grand Prix.Formula 1 reported that Hamilton became emotional after securing the seventh title, saying the scale of the achievement had caused him to “burst into tears.”The result was the biggest sporting reward yet for a journey that had started with his father working multiple jobs to keep him karting.Hamilton’s rise also carried wider importance. He became the first Black driver to compete in Formula 1 and went on to become one of the sport’s most successful drivers. His early experiences with his father helped shape the way he approached both racing and the barriers around it.The story is not simply about a young driver becoming a champion. It is also about the years of work that came before the trophies, contracts and global attention.Anthony Hamilton helped Lewis reach the starting line when the path ahead was far from certain. Lewis then turned that opportunity into one of the greatest careers Formula 1 has seen. Their journey included success, pressure, a difficult professional split and, eventually, a stronger focus on being father and son.For Hamilton, the lessons from those early karting years never disappeared. His father’s work ethic and one simple instruction - “Do your talking on the track” - became part of the way he approached racing and the challenges that came with it.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Players at the US Open in New York are complaining that the smell of marijuana is becoming an unwanted distraction
articles.summary: International Sports News: The 2026 US Open is set to begin on Sunday, but as the world's best players prepare for the year's final Grand Slam, some competitors are dealing with.
articles.body: The 2026 US Open is set to begin on Sunday, but as the world's best players prepare for the year's final Grand Slam, some competitors are dealing with an unexpected distraction around Flushing Meadows: the smell of cannabis drifting in from a nearby park.British players Katie Boulter, Fran Jones and Harriet Dart have all noticed the smell around the USTA Billie Jean King National Tennis Center, with Boulter saying it can affect her concentration during practice and matches.The tournament begins on Aug. 30, with Carlos Alcaraz returning to individual competition for the first time since suffering a wrist injury at the Barcelona Open in April. World No. 1 Jannik Sinner will miss the event with a knee injury, while Novak Djokovic will pursue a record 25th Grand Slam title. Rising star Alex Eala is also expected to receive strong support from New York fans, while Aryna Sabalenka will look to rediscover her best form.Boulter: ‘You don't need distractions’Cannabis is legal for adults aged 21 and over in New York, although smoking is not permitted on the grounds of the tennis center. However, the venue sits beside Corona Park, and the smell can carry across to some practice and outside courts.Boulter, Britain's No. 1 and ranked 60th in the world, said she has encountered it both while practising and during matches.“Yeah, I have experienced it. You go down to the practice courts and down in the park courts, you do smell it a lot,” Boulter said.“But yeah, I'm not a huge fan of it. I know a lot of players have complained on some of the specific courts.“I've played on one before and I did smell it during my match. It's something that I wouldn't like to smell in the middle of my match.“I'm trying to focus and then obviously, it takes you out of the moment and you really don't want to. You don't need distractions. So yeah, I wasn't a huge fan of it.”Jones remembers the smell from last year's US OpenBoulter is not the only British player to have noticed it. Fran Jones, Britain's No. 3, recalled encountering the smell during her first-round match at last year's tournament and said she initially wondered whether it was simply part of playing so close to the park.“Last year I made a joke about that, in my first round, and I said to the guy, 'is this normal?' Because I was on the stadium, and it's next to the park,” Jones said.“He's like, 'yeah.' and I was like, 'well, no wonder I'm playing pretty well.'“This year I'll be like 'no, lock in, lock in!'”Jones, who qualified for this year's tournament, begins her campaign against Poland's Magda Linette on Monday.Harriet Dart, who also came through qualifying, took a more typically New York approach to the situation.“I mean it's New York. It's New York. I feel like everywhere you walk around, it's everywhere, no? It is what it is. Same for everyone,” Dart said.Dart will face American Peyton Stearns in the first round.It has been an issue at the US Open beforeThe smell of cannabis has become a recurring talking point at Flushing Meadows, with players from outside Britain raising similar concerns in previous editions.In 2022, Australian doubles player Nick Kyrgios complained that a spectator smoking courtside was affecting his asthma, prompting the umpire to ask fans to refrain from smoking.A year later, Greece's Maria Sakkari pointed out the smell to the umpire during a match. She later clarified that it was not an excuse for her defeat.Novak Djokovic and Alexander Zverev have also previously noticed the smell around the tournament.The United States Tennis Association, which organises the US Open, has acknowledged the difficulty of dealing with activity taking place beyond the tournament grounds.“While we can't control what takes place off the grounds of the USTA Billie Jean King National Tennis Center, we continue to be vigilant as we maintain this,” the USTA said in a statement.The organisation has said it works with local police and the parks department to address smoking around the boundary of the site.With the 2026 US Open getting under way on Sunday, the cannabis smell is likely to remain a background issue at a tournament already filled with major storylines. Alcaraz will return to action, Sinner will be absent, Djokovic will chase another historic title, Eala will look to make the most of strong local support and Sabalenka will aim to regain her winning form.Boulter will open against American wildcard Carol Young Suh Lee, while Jones and Dart begin their campaigns against Linette and Stearns respectively.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Italian jobs, French connections and Berlin walls: Chess’s European tour
articles.summary: Chess News: For a centuries-old game that has witnessed and survived the rise and fall of empires, kings and kingmakers, chess has developed a vocabulary of its o.
articles.body: For a centuries-old game that has witnessed and survived the rise and fall of empires, kings and kingmakers, chess has developed a vocabulary of its own. This vocabulary is a veritable tour of the people and places that have had major influence on the game.To an ordinary person, 1.e4 c5 is simply a sequence of moves; to a chess player it is the Sicilian Defence. Why Sicily and not Shanghai or St. Louis? Or why Ruy Lopez and not Roy Lampert?I have long been curious to learn the history behind people and places after whom various chess openings and variations are named. One column won’t be enough to cover these places and people; one would have to write an entire book.Europe dominates these places in chess vocabulary. There are historical reasons behind the European dominance, but that is material for another column. In this column, I will write about a few well-known places that many readers may themselves have visited.The Italian JobSicily is well known for Mount Etna, historical ruins and lovely beaches. It is also associated with an often-played move in chess. After 1.e4, Black answers 1...c5, refusing to mirror White in the center and instead attacking it from the side.The Sicilian Defence is played from club level to world championship matches. Its ancestry dates back at least to the Italian theoretician Giulio Cesare Polerio. In a manuscript dating from around 1594, Polerio analysed the sequence 1.e4 c5, making his work one of the earliest known discussions of the opening.Polerio did not name the opening. In 1813, the English writer Jacob Henry Sarratt cited an older Italian source that called it il gioco siciliano (the Sicilian game), helping to establish the term in chess literature.The opening’s reputation was uneven. Some influential theorists dismissed it as an irregular response to 1.e4, while strong nineteenth-century players showed its counterattacking promise.Over time, its eccentricity became its chief appeal: Black does more than defend the center;Black creates imbalance from the first move. The Sicilian Defence is an aggressive counterpunch. It may not always succeed, but then again, neither do all Italian jobs!El MatadorWatching a matador face a raging bull in the rings of Las Ventas in Madrid is an experience you remember for life. Twelve hundred pounds of hulk, armed with two sharp horns, charging at a matador with a singular objective of goring him. The matador deftly moves aside at the last moment with a calm precision.I like to think of Spanish Opening as El Matador for the serenity with which White opens and builds the game against Black.Better known as the Ruy Lopez, the Spanish Opening is one of the foundations of classical opening theory. Its most famous early treatment appeared in Libro de la invencion liberal y arte del juego del axedrez, published at Alcalá de Henares in 1561 by the Spanish priest Ruy López de Segura.López did not invent 3.Bb5; the idea appears in earlier sources, including the Göttingen manuscript from around the late fifteenth century. His contribution was to give the move one of its first systematic analyses. His work proved so influential that the opening came to bear both his name and, across much of Europe, his nationality: the Ruy Lopez, or Spanish Opening.The French ConnectionMy chess journey is intricately linked to France. I have fond memories of that country. I made my first IM norm in Paris and have generally done well in tournaments in France.Named after this wonderful country, the French Defence owes its identity to a correspondence match between Paris and London in 1834, in which members of the Paris team adopted this defensive technique.French Defence looks modest. Black does not immediately challenge White’s pawn on e4. Instead, Black prepares ...d5 by playing 1…e6 and builds a compact central structure. Yet the opening creates exactly the sort of strategic tension that has kept it alive for nearly two centuries.Berlin WallFor almost three decades, the Berlin Wall stood as a symbol of the ideological and geopolitical battles between the two world superpowers. When the wall came down in 1989, the pieces on the geopolitical chessboard were rearranged, followed by the reunification of modern-day Germany.Berlin Defence, also nicknamed Berlin Wall, is one of the old branches of the Spanish Opening. It gets its name from the Berliners who analysed its variations deeply. It is a very defensive opening by Black. So solid that White must work hard to break it down (hence the nickname Berlin Wall).The opening appears in the 1843 edition of Handbuch des Schachspiels edited by Paul Rudolf von Bilguer. It was deployed in the world championship contests in the late 19th century.It went out of fashion for almost a century until Vladimir Kramnik revived it in the 2000 World Championship match against Garry Kasparov. Kramnik played it in four games (all with Black) and frustrated Kasparov with draws in all four games. After losing the championship to Kramnik, Kasparov attributed his loss to Kramnik’s superior preparation with Black. The four openings above are among the best-known of those named after equally well-known Places.Read also: Before AI, there was the Mechanical Turk: The chess machine that wasn’t(Aarav Dengla is India’s 93rd Grandmaster. articles.title: Hrgovic wins IBF world heavyweight boxing title as Itauma hospitalised
articles.summary: Filip Hrgovic is the first Croatian to become a world heavyweight boxing champion after beating Briton Moses Itauma.
articles.body:
Filip Hrgovic of Croatia beat Britain’s Moses Itauma via a ninth-round stoppage to win the vacant International Boxing Federation (IBF) world heavyweight title in a thrilling contest in London.

Itauma, bidding to become the second-youngest heavyweight world champion after Mike Tyson, was on top during the fight’s early stages but had to be carried from the ring on a stretcher and taken to hospital from the O2 Arena on Saturday.

Facing the toughest test of his 15-fight professional career against an experienced Olympic medal winner, the 21-year-old Itauma tired against an opponent with a granite chin.

Itauma’s trainer Ben Davison threw in the towel in the ninth round, but by that time referee Howard Foster had stopped the fight in Hrgovic’s favour as the Croat won the world heavyweight title vacated by Ukrainian boxing great Oleksandr Usyk.

It was Itauma’s first time beyond the sixth round and at one point in the ninth he looked as if he was about to topple.

“I don’t know from where I got energy in that [ninth] round,” said the 34-year-old Hrgovic, almost as spent physically as his beaten opponent.

“It was really not my strength. It was Holy Spirit. He gave me strength in this camp to endure everything, to have [the] best camp of my life, he put me in touch with this great coach Abel Sanchez.”

Hrgovic saluted the courageous Itauma by adding: “I’m the present, and he’s definitely [the] future. He’s an amazing fighter. He’s one of a kind. He’s the best I’ve been in a ring with, but he needed more experience.

“I felt the pace of the fight. I knew I was losing rounds, but I knew that I had that pace in my favour. He was gassing out.”

Itauma landed with several straight left hands early on and Hrgovic was given a standing eight count in the second after being caught with a right hook.

Itauma’s uppercut at the end of the fifth round had home fans in a partisan crowd standing in appreciation.

But come the eighth, both boxers appeared out on their feet, with Hrgovic somehow still standing despite several punishing blows.

Hrgovic was landing powerful shots of his own and, with a dazed Itauma lurching around the ring, Foster called a halt in the ninth round.

Promoter Frank Warren said after the bout that Hrgovic is set to next fight Cuban Frank Sanchez, but the Croatian himself said he instead wants to take on WBO champion Daniel Dubois and then WBC title holder Agit Kabayel — both of whom were ringside at the O2 Arena.

“I want unification. Frank Sanchez will wait,” Hrgovic said.

Hrgovic’s only loss came to Dubois in 2024. Hrgovic was bleeding from deep cuts above his eyes that time when the ringside doctor recommended the fight be stopped.

articles.title: Ethiopia’s Gobena, Kenya’s Olympic champion Jepchirchir win Sydney Marathon
articles.summary: Gobena claims first victory after finishing second last year, as Jepchirchir adds to Boston, New York and London wins.
articles.body:
Ethiopia’s Addisu Gobena and Kenyan world champion Peres Jepchirchir surged to commanding Sydney Marathon wins in the men’s and women’s races .

It was the first victory in a World Marathon Major for 21-year-old Gobena, who came second last year, while Jepchirchir, in Australia on Sunday, added to her previous triumphs in Boston, New York and London.

Gobena made his move in the last kilometre to power home four seconds clear of compatriot Chimdessa Debele Gudeta in 2:04:42. Lesotho’s Tebello Ramakongoana came third.

The dominant run shattered the course record by almost one and a half minutes, with last year’s winner Hailemaryam Kiros dropping from the pace in the dying stages.

“I am very happy,” said Gobena, who was a javelin thrower before transitioning to long-distance running, gaining international attention by winning the 2024 Dubai Marathon.

“Last year I came second, I learnt from my mistake and I went back home and I worked on my mistake to perform and break the record today.”

The unstoppable Jepchirchir was in a league of her own, crossing the finish line in front of the Sydney Opera House in 2:18:31, nearly four minutes ahead of fellow Kenyan Irine Cheptai and Ethiopia’s Shure Demise Ware.

“I was prepared, but I was not sure when I came here if I would win, so I’m so glad and I’m so happy,” said Jepchirchir.

“It was so hilly. First half [of the race] was so tough, but the second was better at least. But it was not easy.”

In the men’s race, the leading pack had thinned to 15 by the halfway mark, with Gobena, world champion Alphonce Simbu and Kiros among them.

Dawit Wolde, Vincent Ngetich and Gobena all attempted breakaways, but they were reeled in by a pack reduced to seven with six kilometres left.

It was still the same group at the 40km mark before Gobena and Gudeta made their move, pulling clear with Gobena outkicking his countryman in the final sprint.

Kenya’s Priscah Cherono went out hard among the women, opening a 20-second gap by 15km and 30 seconds by halfway.

But the lead chasers, down to just Jepchirchir and Cheptai, caught the 46-year-old Kenyan just before 30km.

Jepchirchir and Cheptai eased clear and the relentless world champion then put her foot to the floor, finishing nine seconds off the course record set by Olympic champion Sifan Hassan in 2025.

American Daniel Romanchuk won the men’s wheelchair race, while Switzerland’s Manuela Schar, a three-time Paralympic gold medal winner, took the women’s.

Around 40,000 runners – a record – competed over the picturesque 42.19km course through the city from North Sydney, over the Harbour Bridge to the finish line on the forecourt of the Opera House.

The race was elevated last year to the seventh World Marathon Major, putting it on a par with London, Tokyo, Boston, Berlin, Chicago and New York in the elite global series.

articles.title: Austin FC vs Portland Timbers: 4 takeaways as Verde claim another road win
articles.summary: Oleksandr Svatok scored in stoppage time to give Austin FC a 2-1 win over the Portland Timbers on Saturday at Providence Park.
articles.body:
Austin FC seems to have an edge to itself the last month.

Whether that can spur it to a run over the final stretch of the season to qualify for the MLS playoffs will be fascinating to watch, but Saturday's performance at Portland continues the recent trend that the Verde and Black are on the upswing .

In a game the club probably wouldn't have won before the World Cup break, Austin FC overcame an 89th-minute equalizer by the Timbers and produced a 2-1 win at Providence Park on Oleksandr Svatok 's stoppage-time goal.

"Our guys believe they can get results against any team in the league," Austin FC interim coach Davy Arnaud said. "That's a credit to our guys."

After going 0-8-3 on the road across all eight competitions to start the year, Austin FC has now won two straight MLS road games.

Here are four key takeaways from the match as the Verde and Black (6-10-6, 24 points, 14th West) return home Saturday to host San Jose.

Torres seems to be finding his stride over the past two weeks. As he was Aug. 19 in the win at Seattle, he was excellent Saturday. His goal midway through the first half was a nice, quick shot off a brilliant one-touch pass from Joseph Rosales . Austin FC needs Torres to continue this type of performance to give it a shot at making the playoffs.

Austin FC was the far better side for most of the match, and it would have been a cruel result if the Verde and Black had only gotten one point from the contest. (Portland's goal came on a penalty that was awarded following a shot hitting Brendan Hines-Ike in the arm in the box, which was a stroke of bad luck for Austin FC.)

Austin FC played one of its better 45 minutes of the season in the first half, where it had more possession, dictated the run of play and allowed Portland no scoring chances. Though it wasn't as dominant in the second half, it was still the better team.

"We were really good with the ball tonight and we did a good job of recognizing what we have game-planned for," Arnaud said. "We had such control of the game, which is a collective thing. That adds to the spirit of the group, and there's nothing more important than spirit."

The Verde and Black also didn't crumble mentally when the Timbers tied the game. They were aggressive in stoppage time, which resulted in Svatok's goal inside the six-yard box that came shortly after a corner kick.

"Unbelievable emotions," Svatok said. "I know how important the win is for Austin. It's a great night. … Today we showed how determined we are."

Any overall criticism of the team would be nitpicking, but it was another somewhat quiet performance by forward and designated player Brandon Vazquez .

Moments before Svatok's goal, he missed a cross that would have been an easy tap-in to score. (Though one also has to give credit to Vazquez, as his aggressiveness on the corner kick and positioning on Svatok's shot probably helped throw off Portland goalie James Pantemis on the game-winning score.)

Vazquez wasn't bad, but he still hasn't scored this season, and the club isn't paying him more than $3 million to simply be a solid contributor.

It's another good performance and result for Austin FC, which is now five points out of the ninth and final playoff spot in the Western Conference with 12 games to play.

Winning at Seattle and Portland is difficult, and to do both in an 11-day span is impressive.

The Verde and Black dug themselves a gigantic hole the first half of the season and have a very tough schedule the rest of the way, so if they actually do make a run up the standings, it will be well-earned.

articles.title: Joe Root scripts history vs Pakistan at Lord’s, surpasses Ricky Ponting’s all-time record
articles.summary: Joe Root has made history by scoring the most Test runs for England, eclipsing Ricky Ponting's record in a thrilling match against Pakistan. This landmark no...
articles.body:
Joe Root has added another major record to his remarkable Test career, surpassing Ricky Ponting to become the highest run-scorer in Test history on home soil. The England captain reached the milestone during the second Test against Pakistan at Lord's in London. Root came to the crease on Day 2 and made 24 before Pakistan pacer Mohammad Ali dismissed him lbw. Although Root was unable to turn the start into a substantial innings, those 24 runs were enough to take him past Ponting's long-standing mark. Root now has 7,594 Test runs in England, moving ahead of Ponting's 7,578 runs accumulated in Australia. India's Sachin Tendulkar occupies third place on the list, having scored 7,216 Test runs in India.

Root's latest achievement adds another landmark to a career that has already seen him climb to the top of several major Test batting charts. The England star has reached his 7,594 home runs in 89 Tests and 156 innings, averaging 53.85. His record includes 24 centuries and 35 fifties, with a highest score of 254. Ponting finished his home career with 7,578 runs from 92 Tests and 154 innings at an average of 56.97. The former Australia captain registered 23 hundreds and 38 fifties, with a best of 257. Tendulkar is next on the list with 7,216 runs from 94 Tests and 153 innings in India, while Mahela Jayawardene and Jacques Kallis complete the top five.

Root's record-breaking run at home has also brought renewed attention to another major milestone that remains within his reach. The England batter is currently 1,713 runs behind Tendulkar's all-time Test record of 15,921 runs. Root has scored 14,208 runs in 168 Test matches, while Tendulkar remains at the top of the overall chart. The question of whether Root can eventually overhaul the Indian legend's record is no longer a matter of "if," but "when."

Root's latest milestone came as England continued to hold a commanding position in the second Test against Pakistan, although rain severely restricted the third day's action at Lord's. England reached 177-7 by the close of a disrupted Day 3, taking their overall lead to 357 runs. Only 24.5 overs were possible after showers prevented play during the morning session. The hosts eventually returned in the afternoon with England on 81-3. Dan Lawrence went on to race to an unbeaten 50 from 66 balls before another spell of rain arrived just 14 balls after the teams resumed following tea. There was no further play, with the day eventually abandoned at 6.30pm local time because of bad light. England lost four wickets while adding 96 runs. Emilio Gay was dismissed for 31, Harry Brook fell for 34 and Jamie Smith made seven, with Mohammad Abbas claiming all three wickets to finish the innings with 3-48. Gus Atkinson was then trapped lbw for seven by Mohammad Ali. Lawrence remained unbeaten on 50 alongside Ollie Robinson, who was on two at the close. England had earlier made 290 in their first innings before bowling Pakistan out for 110. The hosts won the opening Test at Headingley by an innings last week and are now looking to seal the three-match series against Pakistan.

articles.title: Spurs fans with pretty special comments before AND after losing at home to Newcastle United
articles.summary: Intriguing reading these comments from Spurs fans both before AND after they faced Newcastle United yesterday. Always an interesting comparison… Spurs fans h...
articles.body:
Intriguing reading these comments from Spurs fans both before AND after they faced Newcastle United yesterday.

Spurs fans have seen their team avoid relegation by only one place in the table in each of the last two Premier League seasons and only stayed up under Roberto de Zerbi on the very final day of last season.

An incredible net spend this summer has seen Tottenham throw cash around for fun.

Yet Newcastle United have put them rock bottom of the Premier League when making it three away wins in a row when visiting Tottenham.

Whist Spurs fans have now seen their team lose at home 14 times against Newcastle United in the Premier League era.

Spurs fans commenting before and facing Newcastle United via their top supporters forum :

'They're a pretty insignificant club but I always want to (and like) beating these

Strange fans, strange reputation given to them by the media as well. Always spoken about as a big club but they've been relegated more times than they've won trophies in the last 70 years

I put them on par with a Brighton or Bournemouth. Lots of local fans but you wouldn't miss them if they go down, and they probably will within the next 5 years.'

'Personally I think we're going to improve massively under De Zerbi and his new squad.

Newcastle have been dismantled, and even though they had a good performance last week, it's probably a tough pill to swallow, and of course we took Tonali .

Where we likely heading is in the opposite direction and a reminder of where they sit in the food chain probably stung as well.

Jealousy raised its ugly head basically.'

'Geordies are no strangers to the second div are they. Only another 70 yrs to wait for the next trophy.'

'They still have Elanga, Wissa, who looks fit again, and Barnes, so they have plenty of pace about them.

Onus will be on us but they look like they have re-stocked well despite the loss of some key players. They will be fine this season and have now got Gonzalez who will give them midfield calm.

It won't be an easy game, even with Osula looking like he is out. Might depend how well Newcastle travel and what this new guy demands of them.'

'Agree though Elanga and their new rb is apparently lightning quick.'

'I think it's very important how we win this. There needs to be flair and we need to make Tottenham and our stadium fun again. Newcastle are still a good side and will have spells but we need to put the football of seasons past behind us and get back to playing beautiful front foot style and being able to open teams up. COYS!!!'

'Means Van Hecke, Van Der Ven and Woltemade can have a non-jump off with each other to see who's worse at timing their headers.'

'The match I dread with half my connected family coming from up there.

4-0 Spurs. I so need us to give them a good pasting to ram down their throats. Especially that slapper Sister in law.

What I've suffered at her hands these last few years is borderline abuse.

'What, are we scared of Wissa and Elanga now?

Had one good game last week, what about the whole of last season.

3-1 Marmoush off the bench for the third to confirm the win.'

'My gut instinct says Tonali needs to get past this game, even though it's at our ground, because their fans are bound to give him stick. No player can like or be unaffected by that.

Hopefully Tonali shows the Newcastle contingent what they lost, and then grows from there.'

'This has got Tonali goal written all over it.

They're pretty sh.. I fancy us to win this handily.'

'Newcastle looked effective v Liverpool, particularly on the break and will press us aggressively which we don't like (see last week). Their quick front line against our pedestrian one is another problem.'

'Newcastle is a must win IMO more so for confirmation and belief that we are on our way back and to set the trend for our home form in this new era.'

'For the first time ever can't really fault the board.

I genuinely think this manager isn't up to it. What evidence do we have that he's any good?

And he's splurged this cash on rejects with no strategy.'

'None but plenty of evidence to suggest he's not good…

Eddie Howe is available and I'd be on the blower tonight if I'm Vinai Venkatesham (CEO at Tottenham).'

'Top 10 should never be acceptable for a club like Tottenham Hotspur.

It isn't acceptable for any other Big 6 club and it shouldn't be for us.

Our aspirations should always be higher. Much higher.

Once the fans start lowering their standards then the football club will follow suit.'

'Tonali definitely needs a rocket shoved up his backside.

I get the pressures of a big money move but he's been truly shocking so far.'

'I thought he looked better in the second half. In all fairness, he couldn't get much worse.'

'Actually passing to our players is already a step up.'

'I know it's early season and I am still optimistic but…Gonzalez totally dominated CMF – and he's half the price of Tonali.

Yes, it takes time to build a time for a team to gel…but Newcastle had a new head-coach who's also new to the PL and they had 3 new players…'

'Fans are fed up and resigned to it in equal measure.

Look how many left early today, soon as it went 2-0 I even turned it off because game was finished.

Many just don't have the confidence or belief that the team can come back from being behind in games because the players ensure that remains the case.'

'Trying not to be all doom and gloom, I thought we controlled the game after the first 10 minutes and it was a ash and grab for Newcastle. But the lack of creativity is a real issue for us.'

Front 3 completely toothless, marmoush will have to score a wonder goal.

All felt very frank like, get the ball to kudus and hope he does something .

Barely laid a glove on them after their second, too many scars off the pitch from the last 2 seasons but also de zerbi is making some very odd decisions.

Finally I'm sick of leaving that stadium having watched us bend over and let the opposition… It's a depressing place to be a home fan.'

'I have made the mistake of finishing work cracking open a beer and coming on here to get a handle on what's going on in the world of Tottenham Hotspur.

I'm forever glad I never had to stand in the trenches with some of you melts.

Fun fact, before today we had lost 6 of our last 8 games against Newcastle. A betting man would have won today.'

'People wonder why players aren't loyal these days – and then you see fans abusing and ridiculing their own player for slipping over, on a wet pitch multiple other players slipped on today.'

'On paper everything sounded perfect! If only we didn't have to actually play games of football.'

'Newcastle weren't brilliant by any stretch of the imagination but they contained us well, keeper made a few good saves and took their chances

What i did find disheartening, was the large number of people who left, with more than 10 minutes left to play – obviously they didn't think we would claw it back.

It still looks a bit disjointed and I'm trying not to get too despondent and having a bit of patience. But this run of defeats cannot continue for much longer'

'I bet Newcastle won't win more than a handful of away games all season.'

'Not so sure about that. He has them set up as a counter attacking side with pace on the break. Think they might actually turn out to be a better side on the road than at Sid James.'

'Jay-Z playing at the stadium next week.

Seriously though. Maybe it all comes down to the fact we're just not a serious football club anymore.

Just a very successful multisports and entertainment venue that also includes a soccer team.

Something is very, very wrong with our club.'

'Why are we weighing in on Tel. Tonali cost three times as much and was utter sh..e.'

'Not sure about Tonali so far but he seems to be unfit?'

'When you spend over £350 million but the refs hate you, it isn't gonna work! Why are Spurs so afraid to call the referees out. They gave them no penalties last season and this season Michael Oliver gave a pen against Spurs in the first match! it's gonna happen again this season only it will be worse. Unless the club speak out…'

'Maybe the club don't speak out because they realise there is no conspiracy against us.'

'Commentary team deep into their "Spurs have spent all this money and are losing, and its great to see Newcastle lose their best players but bounce back" narrative.

You know at this point everyone pretty much hates us. And then cue to cameras on the mass exodus…'

'I thought things couldn't get worse after Frank… boy was I wrong. De Zerbi making Frank look like prime Mourinho.'

'All I hear are excuses about it needs time but a Newcastle team with a new manager and a decimated squad just made us look like Championship fodder.

Most of that team were there last season, essentially the core of it and the attack.'

'I don't think so… the core of their team are at Barca, Woolwich and Spurs. New keeper, new RB, new CM, three other players who were bench warmers for most of last season. You're miles out… try again.'

'Looking forward to relegation honestly, we're a poor team and have been for years. Need a reset.

articles.summary: Cody Gakpo Transfer Latest: Man City Close in on Liverpool Winger as Spurs Miss OutManchester City are moving closer to a major move for Cody Gakpo, with The...
articles.body:
Cody Gakpo Transfer Latest: Man City Close in on Liverpool Winger as Spurs Miss Out

Manchester City are moving closer to a major move for Cody Gakpo, with The Times reporting that Enzo Maresca's side are advancing in their pursuit of the Liverpool winger. The headline claim is clear, City are "close in on £85m-rated Liverpool winger", in what would become one of the standout transfer stories of the window.

The report indicates that Tottenham have missed their chance, with the player having "decides he wants to join Enzo Maresca's side". That detail is likely to shape the conversation around this deal more than the valuation itself. At around £85m, this is a serious proposition, but when a player's preference is established so firmly, the direction of travel can become difficult to alter.

From City's perspective, the interest fits the pattern of targeted recruitment. Gakpo offers versatility across the front line, Premier League experience and a profile suited to high-level possession football. If the situation is as advanced as suggested, Liverpool would face a significant decision over whether to sanction a sale to a direct rival.

There is also a Tottenham angle that adds further intrigue. Spurs are said to miss out on the winger, while the same report adds that "Richarlison also tells De Zerbi he wants to leave north London club". That leaves Roberto De Zerbi facing a potentially awkward reshaping of his attacking options before the new season gathers pace.

For Liverpool, any possible departure of Gakpo would naturally raise questions around succession planning, attacking balance and squad depth under Andoni Iraola. Deals of this magnitude are rarely straightforward, especially between elite domestic competitors, but the language around the player's intention suggests this story has genuine momentum.

Whether City meet Liverpool's demands in full remains to be seen, yet the £85m figure underlines the scale of the situation. If there is room for negotiations, structure and timing may prove every bit as important as the headline fee.

As a confused Liverpool supporter, this one feels hard to process. On one hand, if a report says Gakpo "decides he wants to join Enzo Maresca's side", then you immediately worry that the matter has already moved beyond simple speculation. Once a player's head is turned, things can escalate quickly.

On the other hand, why would Liverpool strengthen Manchester City unless the money is absolutely enormous and there is a crystal-clear replacement lined up? £85m is huge, of course, and nobody can pretend that sort of fee would not make the club think carefully. Still, Gakpo is proven, adaptable and capable of producing in big moments. Selling that profile to a rival always feels risky.

There is confusion too because supporters always try to read between the lines. Is this a genuine push from City? Is it a negotiating tactic somewhere in the market? Or is it simply a case of a high-value player being linked because clubs know his quality? The Spurs detail, that they miss out, does make it sound more advanced than a routine rumour.

From a Liverpool point of view, the biggest concern is what it says about squad stability. Iraola needs clarity, not a prolonged saga around an important attacker. If Gakpo stays, fans will want reassurance. If he goes, fans will demand a top-class replacement immediately. Right now, it feels like one of those stories that creates more questions than answers.

articles.title: Roberto De Zerbi confirms three Spurs stars want to leave
articles.summary: Tottenham transfer window takes hard line as Roberto De Zerbi addresses exitsTottenham’s transfer window has already been one of the busiest in the league, w...
articles.body:
Tottenham transfer window takes hard line as Roberto De Zerbi addresses exits

Tottenham's transfer window has already been one of the busiest in the league, with eight signings completed for almost £400m, and the clear message now is that the churn may not be over. As reported by The Telegraph , Roberto De Zerbi has publicly acknowledged that further movement is expected, and he has done so in language that leaves very little room for sentiment.

After the defeat to Newcastle, attention quickly shifted from the result to the absentees. Richarlison, Kevin Danso and Pape Matar Sarr were all missing, and De Zerbi gave an answer that was striking for its directness. "Richarlison said too many times he wants to leave. Danso came to me two days ago and he said wants to leave and Pape Sarr the same, but he suffered a small injury.

"I love these players. They are great guys. I have very good relationships [with them], but if they want to leave, they have to bring the economic solution to the club, and they can go, and we find other players."

Tottenham transfer window strategy laid bare

This is the modern market in plain terms. Tottenham have spent heavily, they are reshaping the squad at speed, and the head coach is making it clear that desire alone does not force an exit. If players want out, the buying club must meet Spurs' valuation. That is not drama, that is leverage.

Richarlison's situation feels the most advanced simply because De Zerbi framed it as a repeated wish to leave. Danso's request sounds more recent, while Sarr's case appears mixed with a fitness issue. Even so, the wider point is obvious, Spurs are operating without nostalgia.

Richarlison exit could trigger more Spurs deals

For Tottenham, this is now about control. You can let unhappy players go, provided the numbers stack up, and provided replacements are lined up. De Zerbi practically said as much. With so much already spent, Spurs are not in the mood to be dictated to by players or rival clubs trying to negotiate down from a premium fee.

The wider impression is of a club accelerating a rebuild under a coach who wants clarity. Stay and commit, or leave and fund the next move. It is a tough line, but it is coherent, and in a window of this scale that matters more than soft messaging.

As a Spurs supporter, none of this is remotely shocking. In fact, it is overdue. Too often this club has carried players who look half in, half out, and then everyone acts surprised when the team drifts through big moments without edge or conviction. If De Zerbi has decided that anyone agitating for a move can go, fine. Good. That is how serious clubs behave.

The Richarlison update sounds harsh on the surface, but the truth is simple. If a player has made it clear repeatedly that he wants out, why pretend otherwise? Same with Danso, same with Sarr if his head has turned. Spurs should not be a holding pen for players waiting for a better offer elsewhere.

The important part is the phrase about an economic solution. That is the key. Sell if the price is right, replace well, move on quickly. No discounts, no panic, no emotional deals because somebody once scored in a derby or had a good month. Tottenham have already spent close to £400m. That sort of outlay demands ruthless decision-making.

Supporters can live with rebuilding. What they cannot live with is muddle. If De Zerbi is drawing a line early, then fair enough. The squad has to belong to the coach, not to players eyeing the exit. Spurs fans have seen enough false starts. If this is the start of a harder, sharper reset, most will welcome it.

articles.title: Romano reveals how much Man City are ‘set to bid’ for Cody Gakpo after ‘agreement’ with player
articles.summary: Fabrizio Romano has revealed how much Manchester City are reportedly prepared to offer for Cody Gakpo as they aim to execute a headline-grabbing raid on Live...
articles.body:
Fabrizio Romano has revealed how much Manchester City are reportedly prepared to offer for Cody Gakpo as they aim to execute a headline-grabbing raid on Liverpool for the winger.

The Athletic reported on Saturday that the 27-year-old has decided to join Enzo Maresca's side, with all parties now in talks to reach an agreement for the transfer to proceed, and he's opted against joining long-time suitors Tottenham Hotspur.

The Dutchman's prospective exit from Anfield comes at the same time that the Reds close in on the marquee signing of Bradley Barcola from Paris Saint-Germain which could ultimately rise to £123m, making him our second most expensive acquisition of all time.

Late on Saturday night, Romano took to X with an update on Gakpo's situation as Man City prepare to step up their pursuit of the forward in the form of an official offer.

He posted: 'Manchester City are set to bid for £85m package to sign Cody Gakpo after the agreement with player's camp. MCFC stepping up efforts to get the deal done as exclusively revealed tonight. City wait for Liverpool to approve sale when they find replacement.'

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

Selling Gakpo would make Liverpool weaker

Some may argue that it'd be impossible for the Reds to turn down £85m for a player they signed for an initial £37m (potentially rising to £44m, via The Athletic ) in December 2022, especially when he's already 27 and theoretically unlikely to elicit a much higher resale value from hereon.

However, from a footballing perspective, selling one of our most in-form players to a domestic rival with less than 72 hours remaining in the transfer window is near-impossible to comprehend, especially when Andoni Iraola has openly declared that he needs a bigger squad.

Gakpo has begun the season excellently, scoring in the 2-2 draw at Newcastle last week and providing a brilliant assist for Alexander Isak to equalise against Nottingham Forest yesterday, with the Dutchman putting the struggles of last term firmly behind him.

Barcola might be an automatic selection on the left flank once his imminent move from PSG is confirmed, but Liverpool's number 18 has proven capable of playing anywhere across the forward line, impressing on the right against Oliver Glasner's team on Saturday.

In our opinion, there is a place for both of them at Anfield, rather than the arrival of one automatically having to prompt the other's exit. Unfortunately, if Gakpo has decided that he wants to join Man City, there probably isn't a whole lot more the Reds could do to sway him.

This feels like a prospective transfer which could leave LFC with a ton of regrets.

articles.title: Rassie Erasmus hits back at All Blacks over ‘nonsense’ Springboks scrum accusation
articles.summary: All Blacks boss Dave Rennie had accused the world champions of scrummaging illegally before the second Test
articles.body:
South Africa head coach Rassie Erasmus has hit back at New Zealand counterpart Dave Rennie over claims that the Springboks are scrummaging illegally.

The hosts levelled the Rugby's Greatest Rivalry series at 1-1 with a hard-fought win in the second Test in Cape Town, which came after a week of the two sides trading press conference barbs.

All Blacks boss Rennie had suggested that the world champions had been unfairly rewarded during a dominant scrummaging performance even in a 33-16 first Test defeat at Ellis Park, believing that they were walking around and failing to drive straight.

Saturday's scrum-time action was protracted as referee Angus Gardner sought to repeatedly make clear his expectations to the two front rows, with a messy contest nonetheless resulting in few penalties.

And Erasmus believes that Rennie's "moaning" had got into the heads of the officials – before picking out a few bugbears of his own.

"It's the first time in history that people are talking about us walking around," Erasmus insisted. "Why would we all of a sudden walk around? The first six scrums New Zealand had, every single one collapsed and it was reset, reset, reset. Why is it only on their ball that the scrum collapses every single time?

"So don't come with that nonsense and saying we are walking around and trying to put things out in the media. The last lineout was skew. I'm not going to moan my arse off about that. If he's going to start moaning about stuff like that, then they are under pressure.

"Last week we didn't moan when there was clearly a lot of head contacts. Today in the first 40 there were four head contacts and nothing was done about it, and then Lood [de Jager] gets the first one.

"Don't try and convince people through the media. The first week they tried to convince people in the media we were slowing the game down – and we're not. There is obviously a plan to get that message out. We're not going to stay quiet and say, 'ya, we're walking around'. We're not f****** walking around. We are scrumming through.

"We're never ever been accused of walking around. I don't understand it."

Erasmus had tinkered with his line-up at the last moment at Cape Town Stadium, swapping his front rows with the trio of Gerhard Steenekamp, Deon Fourie and Thomas du Toit starting.

Steenekamp and Fourie were removed before half time with Ox Nche and Malcolm Marx – originally named to start – brought on and making a pivotal impact.

Despite defeat, Rennie was happier with the officiating at the set-piece.

"The scrums were better tonight," said Rennie. "I think Angus [Gardner] was pretty strong around setting a mark and trying to keep the hookers in the same sort of spacing. If the Springboks moved across further left, he stopped them.

"We'll give a bit of feedback on that. It's still a bit of an issue for us because they're able to walk around and go straight through our tighthead. There are a couple of technical things we'll share again. In the end both teams were able to play off the scrums and Angus did a reasonable job there."

The series continues on Saturday as the two sides return to Johannesburg for the third Test at FNB Stadium. It will conclude in Baltimore on Saturday 12 September.

articles.title: Former Red Wings Exec Saddened by State of the Team
articles.summary: During his time with the Detroit Red Wings, Neil Smith served as head scout and assistant GM. He ran the […]
articles.body:
During his time with the Detroit Red Wings, Neil Smith served as head scout and assistant GM. He ran the club's farm system.

Smith was instrumental in Detroit's masterful 1989 draft class. It was he who insisted that the team had to draft Sergei Fedorov.

In short, the franchise means a lot to him.

"I have great affection for the Ilitch family," Smith said during the NHL Wraparound Podcast that he co-hosts with Vic Morren.

"Mr. and Mrs. Ilitch bought the team from the Norris family back in 1982, and it has done nothing but go up, up, up in prestige and in value ever since that time. Unfortunately, Mr. Ilitch has since passed, and Mrs. Ilitch is now 93 years old and still hanging in there.

"It's run now by their son Chris Ilitch , who is obviously one of the Ilitch family and has the same brains and acumen."

Smith left the Red Wings to take the position as GM of the New York Rangers. In 1993-94, he led that club to their most recent Stanley Cup win.

However, Smith never lost his affinity for the Red Wings. And that's why he finds the current state of the team to be distressing.

Detroit captain Dylan Larkin has asked for a trade. The club removed Steve Yzerman as GM in July and, with just a few weeks until training camp opens, still doesn't have his replacement in place.

"What I'm really sad about is where the hockey team is right now," Smith said. "Dylan Larkin, a player that has given everything to the Red Wings, played on their last playoff team, is the captain of their team, has told the team way back that he wanted to be traded.

In the Red Wings, Smith Sees A Franchise in Chaos

"That was sad enough. Then Steve Yzerman , a player that I drafted for the Detroit Red Wings , who became general manager after being in Tampa with the same role, has been let go after seven seasons of no playoff hockey. And now we're coming up to the end of August.

"They don't have a general manager. They're still on the lookout for a general manager. I don't know how it's possible that you could be at this point in the summer without a GM.

"The Dylan Larkin saga continues to go on. He's going to have to either expand his list of teams that he'll let Detroit trade him to or just resign himself to the fact that he's coming back to training camp and going to play on the team.

"And until those two things are ironed out— who is the GM and where is Dylan Larkin going to be this year— the team will stay in chaos until those things are figured out. And to me, having worked for that great Original Six team, that's very sad."

The Bianconeri eventually found a way through in the second half, with their substitutes making the difference as they secured a 2-0 victory.

articles.title: Aspiring Lawyer and Taekwondo World Champion, 19, Dies After Suffering Cardiac Arrest in Her Sleep
articles.summary: A family friend described the tragedy as “completely unexpected” in a fundraising page established for the woman’s parents
articles.body:
Isabelle Sava, a 19-year-old aspiring lawyer, died in her sleep on Aug. 17 after suffering an unexpected cardiac arrest

The Queen Mary University of London law student was also an accomplished taekwondo athlete who earned a second-degree black belt and won silver at the 2022 World Taekwondo Championships

Family friend Adriana Agache created a GoFundMe to support Isabelle's parents, Laura and Ovi, adding that Isabelle had "so many plans" and "so much more to give to this world"

An aspiring lawyer and accomplished taekwondo athlete died after suffering an unexpected cardiac arrest .

Isabelle Sava died in her sleep at age 19 on Aug. 17, despite efforts from ambulance and air ambulance crews to resuscitate her, according to a verified GoFundMe established for her parents by family friend Adriana Agache.

In the fundraiser, Agache described Isabelle's death as "completely unexpected," writing that emergency responders "fought desperately to resuscitate her and save her life."

"Tragically, despite everything they did, Isabelle could not be saved," she wrote.

No further details about what caused Isabelle's cardiac arrest were provided.

Isabelle was preparing to begin her second year studying law at Queen Mary University of London and hoped to one day become a lawyer, per the fundraising page.

"She was intelligent, ambitious, focused and incredibly determined," Agache wrote. "She knew where she wanted to go in life, and she was prepared to work hard to get there."

She added that the teen was involved with her university's Law Society, Commercial Awareness Society and Student Advancement Society and served as a student blog writer for the Queen Mary Legal Advice Center.

Isabelle was also an accomplished athlete who had dedicated more than a decade of her life to taekwondo .

After years of training, she earned a second-degree black belt and began competing internationally. In 2022, she competed at the World Taekwondo Championships in the Netherlands, where she won a silver medal in sparring, per Agache and the International Taekwondo Federation .

She also served as a Police Cadet and had completed the Bronze and Silver levels of the Duke of Edinburgh's Award, a U.K. youth development program centered on volunteering, physical activity, skills and expeditions.

However, Agache emphasized that Isabelle was far more than her list of accomplishments.

"Isabelle was kind, intelligent, loving, thoughtful, disciplined, compassionate and incredibly hardworking," she wrote, describing her as "ambitious without being arrogant" and "successful, but humble."

She added that Isabelle was exceptionally close with her parents, Laura and Ovi Sava, noting that she was the couple's only child. She continued to say that Isabelle was Laura and Ovi's "pride and joy," and "best friend."

Agache said that the fundraiser was created so the couple could focus on grieving their daughter and honoring her life without shouldering all of the financial costs that followed her unexpected death.

"Nothing we raise can take away their pain," Agache wrote. "Nothing can replace Isabelle. Nothing can give Laura and Ovi back the future they should have shared with their daughter. But together, we can surround them with love, kindness and support and take at least one burden from their shoulders during the darkest time of their lives."

"Isabelle had so many plans. So many dreams. So much potential. And so much more to give to this world," Agache continued, adding, "Her story should have had so many more chapters."

Trenic TKD, a U.K.-based network of Taekwon-Do academies, shared a tribute to Isabelle on Instagram on Aug. 21.

"It is with deep sadness and heavy hearts that we share the devastating news of the passing of Isabelle Sava," the organization wrote in its tribute.

"Beyond her remarkable achievements on the mats, Isabelle was a pleasure to teach, train alongside, and know. She will be sorely missed by everyone who had the privilege of meeting her across the Taekwon-Do community. Our deepest thoughts, love, and prayers are with her family and friends during this heartbreaking time," it added.

articles.title: Arsenal Cannot Afford to End the Window With a Weaker Attack
articles.summary: Gooners of a certain age will know the company line Mr Wenger used to quote at the end of every transfer window.The recruitment policy at Arsenal apparently...
articles.body:
Gooners of a certain age will know the company line Mr Wenger used to quote at the end of every transfer window.

The recruitment policy at Arsenal apparently was to only target players who could make the squad dramatically better. So, when we got to deadline day and the club had been unsuccessful in landing the big name on their shortlist, a fanbase was meant to be comforted by the notion that they had tried.

Between now and Tuesday, the Gunners and Atletico Madrid might try to call Julian Alvarez's bluff to see if the 26-year-old really is willing to stay in the Spanish capital and wait for his employers to have a change of heart regarding negotiating with Barcelona.

Yet there is every chance that Mikel Arteta is telling us next week that the Champions only want an individual who can make them better, that such a player is hard to find in the market, and that he is happy with what he's been left with.

Andrea Berta might have enough credit in the bank. While he will never publicly confirm or deny it, maybe he did have a lucrative contract ready for Vinicius Jr., and maybe he's ready to pounce if Alvarez is convinced to move back to England.

Yet wanting something isn't the same as getting something, and our director of football is paid a lot of money to give our manager the best resources to work with.

The Italian has had months to identify names who could have improved our attack, and if he's being judged as ruthlessly as players are, you have to say that saying you tried really wouldn't be good enough.

In a sport where everyone talks to each other off record, the 54-year-old at the very least needs an alternative shortlist – a list of those who can replace Martinelli if your idealistic choice isn't available.

Chelsea signed Rodgers, Liverpool are about to buy Barcola, Nico Williams has a release clause, Rashford is available, etc.

So, while there is empathy that it's hard to finalise deals for world-class talent, not having a Plan B wouldn't be acceptable.

Arsenal should improve from a position of strength

When you lift the Premiership, that's a position of strength you're meant to improve from. Others in our position would. They wouldn't consider reducing their offensive weapons without a replacement lined up.

Even from a business point of view, for what we pay for merchandise and tickets, don't we deserve to see the team we love strive to improve?

If our attack this time next week is weaker than last season, then that's not okay.

What do you think, Gooners? Would it be unacceptable for Arsenal to finish the transfer window with a weaker attack than last season, or should we trust Arteta and Berta if their preferred targets simply aren't available? Let us know in the comments.
