articles.body:
Sights from the first Ball State football 2026 fall camp practice

Ball State football season is just a week away, so it's time to break down the Cardinals' schedule with our game-by-game predictions.

Ball State is coming off a 4-8 season in head coach Mike Uremovich's debut campaign. The Cardinals have not won six games to qualify for bowl eligibility since 2021 and have not won a bowl game since 2020, which is also the last year the Cardinals won the Mid-American Conference.

Will Uremovich lead the Cardinals to the postseason in year two? Here's what we think will happen with Ball State football in 2026:

The Cardinals will open their season on the road against one of the giants of the sport. Ohio State is the No. 1 ranked team in the preseason Coaches Poll and AP Poll, and the Buckeyes are loaded with future NFL talent like superstar receiver Jeremiah Smith. An upset by little ol' Ball State would immediately become one of the greatest in the history of the sport, but Cardinals fans shouldn't get their hopes up.

Prediction: Ohio State 56, Ball State 7 . Cardinals are now 0-1.

Ball State's home opener will pit the Cardinals against Stony Brook, an FCS team that plays in the Coastal Athletic Association. Ball State's last two FCS opponents — New Hampshire in 2025 and Missouri State in 2024 — gave them all that they could handle, but Stony Brook hasn't had as much recent success as those two programs did entering those matchups. The Cardinals pick up their first victory in front of the home crowd.

Prediction: Ball State 31, Stony Brook 15. Cardinals are now 1-1.

The nonconference slate continues with a road trip to Lynchburg, Virginia, where Ball State will take on Liberty. The Flames have been one of the most successful Group of Five/Six programs since moving up to the FBS ranks with six bowl appearances and a Conference USA championship in the last seven years, but they matched Ball State's 4-8 record last year in their worst FBS season yet. However, Liberty is more well-resourced than your typical G6 programs, and they have the means to reload on talent for a bounce-back season. Ball State made things interesting on the road at UConn last season and could do the same this year, but it's tough to imagine Liberty's slump lasting longer than one season.

Prediction: Liberty 27, Ball State 21. Cardinals are now 1-2.

The MAC season begins with a road trip to Kent State. The Golden Flashes won just one game combined in the 2023 and 2024 seasons but showed rapid improvement under head coach Mark Carney, who led them to a 5-7 record and 4-4 MAC record in 2025. Kent State nearly beat Ball State in Muncie last year, and the Golden Flashes return starting QB Dru DeShields (2,030 yards with 18 TDs and 3 INTs) along with several other offensive weapons. With more continuity and home field advantage, Kent State gets its first win over Ball State since 2019.

Prediction: Kent State 20, Ball State 17. Cardinals are now 1-3 (0-1 MAC).

Toledo has been one of the most consistent programs in the MAC this century, having not posted a losing record since 2009. However, the Rockets are in a period of transition after longtime coach Jason Candle left to take over at UConn, leaving former Mercer head coach Mike Jacobs to take over. Toledo still has plenty of talent and will likely be favored entering this game, but the Cardinals pull off an early-season upset similar to last year's MAC opener against Ohio.

Prediction: Ball State 25, Toledo 24. Cardinals are now 2-3 (1-1 MAC).

Ball State's final nonconference game will take the Cardinals to Evanston, Illinois, for another Big 10 opponent. While Northwestern is a far less formidable foe than Ohio State, the Wildcats still put up big numbers against the Cardinals in their brand-new stadium.

Prediction: Northwestern 38, Ball State 13. Cardinals are now 2-4 (1-1 MAC).

Bowling Green is in a similar spot to Ball State, as both programs are coming off 4-8 seasons under new head coaches. The Falcons only have six returning starters and a young roster, so they are a bit of an enigma as far as MAC teams go. Head coach and Pro Football Hall of Famer Eddie George brought in the MAC's top-ranked recruiting class, but it's probably too early for them to make a big impact on this one. Ball State overcomes last season's road jitters and survives a surprising shootout to get the first road win over the Uremovich era.

Prediction: Ball State 38, Bowling Green 34. Cardinals are now 3-4 (2-1 MAC).

The newest member of the MAC will pay a visit to Muncie just before the schedule shifts into midweek MACtion mode. The possibility of a "Ball-Sac Bowl" has gone viral on social media ever since Sacramento State joined the conference as a football-only member, and the internet is sure to be ablaze with some crass humor leading up to this game. Perhaps that viral attention stokes the flames of a new rivalry and motivates the Cardinals to put together a dominant showing.

Prediction: Ball State 31, Sac State 13. Cardinals are now 4-4 (3-1 MAC).

Ball State's first MACtion game of the season will send the Cardinals to Amhert, Massachusetts, to take on another one of the conference's newer members. UMass joined the MAC in all sports ahead of the 2025-26 academic year, but its first football season in the conference did not bode well as the Minutemen finished 0-12. They are expected to remain one of the worst teams in college football this season, and Ball State takes advantage of it on national TV.

Prediction: Ball State 24, UMass 14. Cardinals are now 5-4 (4-1 MAC).

After a long road trip to the Northeast for their first MACtion game, the Cardinals will return home to host another Northeastern MAC foe. Former Ball State coach Pete Lembo is now the head coach at Buffalo and will return to Muncie for the first time since resigning as the Cardinals coach in 2015. The Bulls were expected to be one of the better teams in the conference last year but finished in the middle of the pack and lost a majority of starters on both sides of the ball. The Cardinals take down a rebuilding team and clinch bowl eligibility with their sixth win.

Prediction: Ball State 17, Buffalo 13. Cardinals are now 6-4 (5-1 MAC).

Ball State's final MACtion game will send it on the road to Athens, Ohio, where the Bobcats will have a first-year head coach in John Hauser. Like Toledo, the Bobcats have been one of the better programs in the conference with at least nine wins and a bowl victory in each of the last four years. Ohio will also be out for revenge after an early-season loss in Muncie last year likely cost them a shot at the MAC Championship.

Prediction: Ohio 29, Ball State 17. Cardinals are now 6-5 (5-2 MAC).

The regular season finale brings the Cardinals back to Muncie to take on Central Michigan. The Chippewas qualified for a bowl game last year under first-year head coach Matt Drinkall and return most of their starting offensive line and weaponry. The defense presents a lot more question marks after losing a lot of veteran production, and by this point in the season, Ball State's offense is grooving. The Cardinals finish the year undefeated at home after an exciting game.

Prediction: Ball State 42, Central Michigan 38. Cardinals are now 7-5 (6-2 MAC).

Monday, Dec. 21, vs. North Dakota State in Famous Idaho Potato Bowl

Ball State just misses out on the MAC Championship but qualifies for its first bowl game since 2021 by winning seven games. The Famous Idaho Potato Bowl typically features a Mountain West team vs. a MAC team, so we're projecting a matchup with North Dakota State, a first-year MWC program which just made the jump to FBS after years as an FCS dynasty. The Bison remain a formidable program despite making that division jump and send the Cardinals home from Boise disappointed.

Prediction: NDSU 27, Ball State 14. Cardinals finish 7-6 (6-2 MAC).

articles.title: Baker, Freeport, Walton highlight Week 2 high school football wins
articles.summary: After two weeks of HS football, only SoWal and Walton are 2-0 in the area while Baker, Freeport bounced back in big ways Friday. Our Week 2 roundup.
articles.body:
South Walton football shuts out FWB, improves to 2-0

It's really impressive what's going on in Walton County.

South Walton and Walton's defenses have yet to allow a touchdown, Freeport is running down people's throats and is a couple of flags away from being 2-0 and the three are a combined 5-1. Meanwhile in Okaloosa County, Choctaw and Crestview's tough schedules have resulted in 0-2 starts, and Destin, Fort Walton Beach, Baker and Niceville are each 1-1, the latter two bouncing back this past week with wins.

Here's a rundown of the week (with links to FWB-SoWal, Niceville-West Florida below):

Dylan Louthain rushed for five touchdowns to match a program record, and Freeport got its first win of the Bobby Johns era on the road.

Louthain had four touchdowns alone in the first half following a Dylan Molstead touchdown plunge to begin the night. Out of the halftime locker rooms leading 34-20, Carter Nunes connected with Talen McElyea for a 22-yard touchdown, and then Louthain capped off his prolific night with a 32-yard touchdown run to break the 200-yard rushing mark. According to Blake McCormick, Louthain joined Keith Williams (1993) and Brandon Siples (2019) as the program record holders with five touchdown runs in a game.

To cap things off, Colin Spiva scored his first varsity touchdown. Freeport (1-1) travels to winless Gulf Breeze next week.

Calvin Wilks piled up 176 yards and three touchdowns on 31 carries, Dawson Mitchem ran for 106 yards and two scores and had 179 overall yards and the Gators embraced home field and routed a Destin program coming off a 53-13 win over Port St. Joe.

Now 1-1, Matt Brunson's crew travels to 2-0 Holmes County Friday, Sept. 4, while Destin hosts winless North Bay Haven in a game in which the Sharks will be heavily favored.

Buying into the 6:30 a.m. workouts, none of which a varsity play has missed all year. Buying into the coach's veteran leadership. Buying into the collective thought that last year's 4-7 rebuild left a bad taste in everyone's mouth.

Two games in, Walton has two redemption wins and a 93-13 margin of victory, the latest a running-clock win at home over an Arnold team that just beat district rival Freeport.

Eli Odom found the end zone, Whitton West and Rodney Clinch each had two touchdowns and Tristian Powell also scored for the Bulldogs, who have an off week before hosting Taylor County (1-1) on Sept. 11.

Everybody knew Choctaw's early season schedule was brutal. An 0-2 start has affirmed that for the defending Region 1-4A champs, who have yet to put it all together in the wake of graduating most of their vaunted defense and dealing with a quarterback change.

Friday saw all three quarterbacks play at Joe Etheredge Stadium, Carter Marracco flashing his speed with two touchdown runs (68, 12) and Isaiah Collins replacing starter Baker Giles in the second half with a touchdown toss. The switch was not enough to come back from a 21-7 halftime deficit.

It doesn't get it any easier next week when the Big Green host Pace (1-1), which lost 51-33 to Pensacola Catholic Friday night.

The Bulldogs' strength of schedule is showing early on, the Bulldogs still in search of their first win after being humbled by the same Enterprise team that handed Choctaw its lone regular-season loss last year.

The Bulldogs look to right the ship Thursday, Sept. 3, when they host 1-1 Pine Forest (1-1), which shut out Escambia 8-0 Friday night.

The Raiders fell to 0-2 but will again have a winnable contest Friday, Sept. 4, against 0-2 Milton at Bennett C. Russel Stadium.

articles.title: CBS names Titans former second round pick as top candidate to get cut
articles.summary: In a recent article from CBS, they named former second round pick, Tennessee Titans quarterback Will Levis, as a top candidate to get cut.
articles.body:
There was once a time when quarterback Will Levis was thought to be the future of the Tennessee Titans . Now, as the third-string quarterback behind Cam Ward and Mitch Trubisky, Levis faces the possibility of getting cut. In fact, according to an article from CBS , Levis a top candidate among veterans to get cut before the Titans finalize their 53-man roster. Here is what they had to say:

"There was a brief period when Will Levis was supposed to be the Titans ' franchise quarterback. Three years after Tennessee made him the first player off the board on Day 2 of the 2023 draft, he could be out the door. It comes down to whether the Titans will carry two quarterbacks or three. Cam Ward is the face of the franchise, and Trubisky is the clear choice to be his backup given his familiarity with Brian Daboll's scheme. If this first-year staff only wants two quarterbacks, the Levis experience is over."

It comes down to whether the Titans will carry two quarterbacks or three. Cam Ward is the face of the franchise, and Trubisky is the clear choice to be his backup given his familiarity with Brian Daboll's scheme. If this first-year staff only wants two quarterbacks, the Levis experience is over."

In head coach Robert Saleh's history when he served as the head coach of the New York Jets, he tended to keep three quarterbacks on the roster if he had confidence in all of them. So, Levis should have a role on the roster if he has done enough to convince the coaches to keep him around. However, throughout training camp and their first two preseason games, Levis has failed to impress, which could put his roster spot in jeopardy.

Perhaps his final chance to prove to the coaching staff why he should stay on the roster was in Tennessee's final preseason game against the Chicago Bears on Saturday. He completed 14 of 22 passes for 143 yards. It was the final game of the NFL preseason before every team finalizes its initial 53-man roster on Sunday.

articles.title: 4 potential surprise cuts by Commanders: 2 rookie draft picks in danger?
articles.summary: The Commanders must trim their roster to 53 players by Sunday evening. We examine four potential surprise cuts.
articles.body:
The Washington Commanders have until 6:00 p.m. Sunday to trim their roster from 90 to 53 players. The work has already begun , as Washington reportedly released five players on Saturday.

Of the first five moves, none were surprises. Washington released two safeties, two linebackers and an offensive lineman. The Commanders are deep at the first two positions, and Nicholas Petit-Frere, the offensive lineman released, was always a long shot when he signed during training camp.

Washington made its most surprising cut last week, releasing veteran safety Will Harris. However, if you'd been to Commanders training camp or watched Harris in action, it wasn't much of a surprise. He had struggled. His release likely means Washington is set at safety with Nick Cross, Jeremy Reaves, Quan Martin, Tyler Owens and Percy Butler.

Speaking of surprise cuts, could the Commanders move on from 2024 third-round pick Luke McCaffrey? Washington had six receivers inactive for the preseason finale at Baltimore on Friday, which usually indicates a player is safe. Two players competing for a spot at receiver, McCaffrey and Van Jefferson, were active. What does it mean? It means McCaffrey isn't 100% safe, despite a solid training camp.

Let's look at four potential surprise cuts on Sunday and why it would be a surprise.

Look, even with McCaffrey playing on Friday night, it would still be a bit of a surprise if he were cut. Washington's fan base is weirdly split on McCaffrey. Some believe he should be a superstar, even though he was the No. 100 overall pick in 2024. When the Commanders selected McCaffrey, he'd only played wide receiver for two years. Last season, McCaffrey appeared to be making strides, taking over as Washington's primary kickoff returner, averaging 30 yards per return. He also caught three touchdowns before breaking a collarbone in Week 9. McCaffrey can play inside or outside. The Commanders were trying multiple players at kick returner this summer, so were they looking for potential replacements? McCaffrey is the player to watch on Sunday.

When the Commanders used a sixth-round pick on running back Kaytron Allen in April's NFL draft, many believed he'd be the short-yardage and goal-line back in 2026. Allen isn't a dynamic back, but he's productive. He finished his career as Penn State's all-time leading rusher. In Washington's first preseason game, he carried the ball 23 times without one negative rush. According to Warren Sharp, he was the only running back over the last decade to have 20+ carries and not lose a single yard on any of his attempts. Allen is known for protecting the football, but in the preseason finale, he fumbled on Washington's first snap from scrimmage and later bobbled a kickoff. The Commanders like Allen, but could they try to sneak him through to the practice squad? If another team did claim him, it's not hard to find backs like Allen. Undrafted rookie Robert Henry Jr. offers a more dynamic skill set.

Another of Washington's 2026 draft picks, does GM Adam Peters believe he could also get Gulbin through to the practice squad? The rookie had his moments this summer, but he also faced his share of struggles. You can bet Peters will be searching hard for veteran interior offensive line help, either through the trade market or from players waived by other teams. The Commanders would like to develop Gulbin, but he has some limitations. If they waive Gulbin, that doesn't mean Julian Good-Jones is making the roster. It would signal that Washington has found veteran help elsewhere. I'd expect Good-Jones to be released with Gulbin making the roster as an interior reserve. But the Commanders absolutely cannot go into Week 1 with Gulbin as the primary backup center.

Trent Scott has enjoyed a successful NFL career. An undrafted free agent in 2018, Scott is entering his ninth NFL season. He's appeared in 96 NFL games and made 26 starts. He's been with Washington since 2023. He'll always be the answer to the trivia question of 'Who caught Jayden Daniels' first career touchdown pass?' Scott's flexibility also helps his cause, as he can play guard and tackle. However, he played late in Friday's loss to the Ravens and struggled. He struggled against players who are unlikely to make NFL rosters in 2026.

Still, the Commanders like Scott. He's dependable and can fill in for them in a pinch. Because he can play multiple spots, he's almost always active. Unless Peters can find help elsewhere, Scott will be hard to knock off the roster, considering Washington's current issues. So, it would be a surprise if he's cut. Of course, I would expect the Commanders' offensive line could look much different before Week 1.

articles.title: Kansas State football opens the Collin Klein era this week vs Nicholls
articles.summary: An offseason of celebration around Collin Klein's return to Kansas State football is almost over. The Wildcats open against Nicholls this weekend.
articles.body:
MANHATTAN — To the tune of the famous opening riff of Wolfmother's Joker and the Thief, Collin Klein emerged from the southwest tunnel of Morgan Family Arena, reintroducing himself to the Kansas State faithful , this time as the Wildcats' head coach.

Perhaps the most beloved player in the history of the Wildcats football program was home. A two-year stint as Texas A&M's offensive coordinator prepared him for a moment that he dreamt of since his first visit to the Manhattan campus nearly two decades before. That visit launched a playing career that made him a Heisman Trophy finalist en route to a Big 12 title, before he returned as an assistant and helped lead the Wildcats to another conference championship.

"I told our players this afternoon that they're going to get every ounce that I have to help move this program forward in every single area," Klein said on that December afternoon . "I love challenges; I love going and doing hard things. To take this program where it has never been is going to be hard, and I want it to be hard. We are going to attack this thing together, as a staff, as players, as a fanbase and as an administration... We're going to take this program where it hasn't been before."

Photos from Kansas State football fall camp practice

An offseason of celebration followed, and Klein and his new staff won on the recruiting trail in ways K-Staters aren't used to. At the same time, the team prepared for a year with high expectations and the chance to contend for a championship in the Big 12 Conference.

Come Saturday, Sept. 5, Klein will run out of the northwest tunnel of Bill Snyder Family Stadium, leading the Wildcats as head coach for the first time. To the tune of the famous opening riff of Wolfmother's Joker and the Thief, the opening kick of Kansas State 's new era will commence, officially starting the 2026 season and an exciting new era of Wildcats football.

"I've been a part of this program at every level, from recruit to player to graduate assistant to position coach to coordinator to, now, head coach," Klein said. "To be able to carry on the legacy of the incredible head coaches that have been here before is a little surreal, but I'm still very honored."

Collin Klein replaced Chris Klieman as Kansas State football coach

Reports emerged on the morning of what was supposed to be a regular National Signing Day in early December that Chris Klieman was retiring as the Wildcats' coach after a 6-6 season. Those reports also connected Klein to his alma mater after a successful two-year stint at Texas A&M, where he solidified his reputation as one of college football's better playcallers.

Klein and Klieman later said that the outgoing coach called his former offensive coordinator and told him to hold off on accepting another job, believed to be at South Florida, because Kansas State was about to open. Athletic director Gene Taylor said that when Klieman informed him of his retirement, he told his boss it was time to bring Klein home.

It happened quickly. Klieman announced his retirement on the evening of National Signing Day, and Klein was officially named the Wildcats' coach the next day, signing a five-year contract with an average base salary of $4.3 million. He was introduced at Morgan Family Arena the day after.

"God's timing is perfect with how everything went down, and I couldn't be more grateful to be home," Klein said moments after his plane touched down . "This is family. I'm lost for words."

Collin Klein turning in early big wins on recruiting trail

A celebration followed Klein into the offseason, as he continued to win over the fanbase's belief through his recruiting victories. A busy transfer portal window in January saw him land new weapons for quarterback Avery Johnson, along with potential defensive standouts like Wendell Gregory and Mekhi Mason.

When Klein turned his attention to the 2027 recruiting class, he won in ways Kansas State has never seen before .

With 29 players committed, Kansas State currently has a consensus Top 30 class, which includes the top in-state prospect and multiple four-star prospects. Some three-stars are knocking on the door of becoming four-star prospects, while the class only trails Texas Tech within the Big 12. The class is trending toward one of the best, if not the best in program history.

"I tell them it's gonna be hard; I tell them that it's a badge of honor to wear that Powercat, and the most valuable things in your life, you're gonna have to pay the most for, and we're gonna make that price really freaking high to play at K-State," Klein said at Big 12 Media Days . "Guys are attracted to that, and the right guys will be attracted to that."

Kansas State enters 2026 season with high expectations

A transformational offseason finally brings Kansas State into a game week, with Kansas State opening against Nicholls at 6 p.m. on Saturday at Bill Snyder Family Stadium. An expected sold-out crowd under the stadium's new LED lights will begin a new era, while fans hope the play on the field will keep the party going.

The Wildcats have high expectations in 2026. Johnson is back as K-State's starting quarterback for his third season. They hope the weapons around him are upgrades, while the defense has much room for improvement after the 2025 campaign. A favorable draw in the Big 12 schedule could have the Wildcats in contention, while they enter the year with the fourth-best odds to win the league.

It won't go without its challenges. Kansas State's offensive line has already taken a big hit with All-Big 12 tackle John Pastore out for the season, which will lead to a completely new starting unit. The defense has multiple personnel questions. Johnson also needs to take a step forward.

Those questions will soon be answered when Klein walks out of the tunnel, and the guitar riff to Joker and the Thief sounds over the stadium's speakers. An offseason of anticipation will finally reach its end.

"This place is home; this place is family," Klein said. "I still have to pinch myself sometimes because it's so special."

articles.title: Gattuso to Make Three Changes to Lazio Starting Lineup Against Genoa
articles.summary: Lazio head coach Gennaro Gattuso will reportedly make a trio of changes to his starting lineup when they host Genoa on Sunday, including two compulsory ones....
articles.body:
Lazio head coach Gennaro Gattuso will reportedly make a trio of changes to his starting lineup when they host Genoa on Sunday, including two compulsory ones.

Lazio Aiming for a Home Victory Against Genoa

The Biancocelesti began their Serie A campaign with an away victory in Bologna thanks to Davide Frattesi's solitary strike . The Italian midfielder came off the bench to replace the injured Fisayo Dele-Bashiru. The manager also had to make another compulsory change during the match, bring in Romano Floriani Mussolini for Adam Marusic.

Frattesi & Floriani Mussolini to Start in Lazio vs Genoa Clash

With both players expected to remain on the sidelines for at least 20 days , Frattesi and Floriani Mussolini will be making their first starts of the season. The Inter Milan loanee will join Kenneth Taylor and Nicolo in the midfield trio, while Floriani Mussolini will slot in at right-back, with the rest of the defence remaining intact with Danilo Doekhi, Oliver Provstgaard, and Alfonso Pedraza.

Gattuso to Choose Between Matteo Cancellieri & Gustav Isaksen

In attack, Sky Sport Italia and La Lazio Siamo Noi expect a third change to take place, with Gustav Isaksen dropping Matteo Cancellieri to the bench. The Dane missed the entire pre-season while recovering from groin surgery, but made his return in the second half at the Renato Dall'Ara and was considered an upgrade on his Italian teammate .

Gustav Isaksen (Photo by Marco Rosi – SS Lazio/Getty Images)

On the contrary, La Gazzetta dello Sport believes Cancellieri remains the slight favourite (60%) to start ahead of Isaksen (40%). All sources agree that Mattia Zaccagni and Boulaye Dia should complete the attacking trident, but GdS leaves a 40% chance for Andrea Pinamonti to make his Lazio debut from the start at the Senegalese's expense.

Gattuso remains without long-term absentees Samuel Gigot, Patric, and Danilo Cataldi, in addition to Luca Pellegrini and the previously mentioned Marusic and Dele-Bashiru. On the other hand, Alessio Romagnoli and Josip Sutalo's conditions are improving, so it remains to be seen if they will receive call-ups against Genoa.

Lazio Probable XI (4-3-3): Mandas; Floriani Mussolini, Doekhi, Provstgaard, Pedraza; Frattesi, Rovella, Taylor; Isaksen, Dia, Zaccagni

articles.title: ✅ Arrival confirmed at Stamford Bridge, Chelsea sign Dibu Martínez
articles.summary: Aston Villa officially confirmed the departure of Emiliano 'Dibu' Martínez. The historic Argentine goalkeeper was sold outright to Chelsea, bringing an unfor...
articles.body:
Aston Villa officially confirmed the departure of Emiliano 'Dibu' Martínez . The historic Argentine goalkeeper was sold outright to Chelsea, bringing an unforgettable spell in Birmingham to a close as he takes a massive step forward within English football.

The Mar del Plata native arrived at the 'Villans' in 2020 from Arsenal and quickly made the goal his own. Through impossible saves and fierce leadership, he became the standout figure of a team that reached the pinnacle by winning the UEFA Europa League last May.

His time at Villa Park was the perfect springboard for his rise with the Argentina National Team . Wearing the albiceleste, Dibu reached the very top: he won two Copa América titles and the unforgettable World Cup in Qatar 2022, playing a decisive role in penalty shootouts.

Individual recognition soon followed for the No. 1. The Argentine won the Yashin Trophy twice (2023 and 2024) and claimed two FIFA The Best awards, cementing his status as the best goalkeeper on the planet.

From the English club, he was bid farewell with eternal gratitude for his competitive spirit and his indelible mark. Now, Dibu takes on a hugely prestigious challenge at Stamford Bridge, where he will look to make the 'Blues' goal his own.

Amid speculation over his future, Matias Fernandez-Pardo (21) was omitted from Lille OSC's matchday squad to face Paris Saint-Germain on Friday night. There have also been reports that the Belgian has been absent from training and, as per a report from Foot Mercato, he may have played his final game for the Ligue 1 side.

Fernandez-Pardo has been linked with an exit from LOSC all summer. Newcastle United have been the keenest suitor for the Belgium international, who competed at this summer's FIFA World Cup. However, for much of the window, there has been a significant gap in the player's valuation between the two clubs. However, Foot Mercato understands that there has now been a breakthrough.

With the end of the transfer window nearing, Newcastle United have stepped up talks for the forward. An agreement is now close, with the Premier League side close to LOSC's valuation for the player.

articles.body:
Dundee United reportedly agree a fee for Vicko Sevelj to join Neftci Baku as St Mirren appear poised to sign a Serbian striker on Sunday and Monaco are linked with Rangers' Djeidi Gassama.

Vicko Sevelj missed Dundee United's win over Kilmarnock on Saturday as the 25-year-old utility man was given permission to travel to the Azerbaijani capital for a medical and contract talks after a fee was agreed for his transfer to Neftci Baku . ( The Courier )

Anderlecht have reignited their interest in Will Ferry and are in negotiations with Dundee United for the 25-year-old left-back. ( Sacha Tavolieri on X )

Venezuela striker Kevin Kelsy is awaiting a UK visa, medical and work permit before the 22-year-old completes his transfer from Portland Timbers to Rangers . ( Ekrem Konur on X )

‌Kevin Kelsy will not be phased by the £9m price tag when the "strong, powerful striker" completes his move to Rangers , according to Portland Timbers coach Liam Ridgewell. ( Daily Record )

Ferencvaros have told Rangers they are looking for at least £5.1m for 25-year-old Haiti striker Lenny Joseph and other clubs are also monitoring the situation. ( Foot Mercato )

Rangers have told Monaco it would need a bid of more than £8.5m to persuade them to sell Djeidi Gassama after offers of around £6m from Monza and Parma were rejected for the 22-year-old winger. ( Foot Mercato )

Wolverhampton Wanderers manager Cesar Peixoto has told 33-year-old England international goalkeeper Sam Johnstone, who is under consideration by Celtic , he is not part of his plans. ( Glasgow Times )

St Mirren have struck a deal to sign striker Niko Agrafiotis from German third-tier outfit Wehen Wiesbaden and the 26-year-old is set to make his debut against Motherwell on Sunday after passing a medical. ( Scottish Sun )
